synthetic_samples.reference_summary: At 09:22, a synthetic tree branch contacted feeder 47's primary conductor, causing relay 52-47 to open. The SCADA operator at Synthetic Control initiated remote closing of feeder breaker 52-47 at 09:31 after repairs were reported complete. The ground relay 51G-47's pickup was set to 150 amperes, while the magnetizing inrush produced 1.9 kiloamperes. Relay 27-47's undervoltage block was configured to release after 1 second, matching the dead-line check time exactly. After the 1.9 kiloampere inrush exceeded pickup, relay 51G-47 issued a trip command in 45 milliseconds. The distribution management system locked out feeder 47, stopping the restoration sequence and blocking remote closure. The failed restoration left 1,400 Synthetic customers without power for three hours, undercounted as a 12 megawatt-hour outage. No physical equipment was damaged because the 200 millisecond backup interrupter removed the false fault before thermal stress. Engineers uploaded corrected settings to relay 51G-47, raising pickup to 500 amperes with harmonic restraint enabled. Only if a zero-voltage check remains true for 20 seconds will breaker 52-47 reclose after a lockout.

synthetic_samples.reference_summary: At 13:05, lightning struck Synthetic North Feeder 9, causing a phase-to-phase fault and tripping the feeder breaker. After a successful 80 second dead-line test, operators issued an automatic restoration sequence at 14:22. The neutral overcurrent relay 51N-9 had a pickup of 240 amperes, which is less than the capacitor inrush. The restoration logic allowed breaker 52-9 to close while bus residual voltage remained at 35 percent. The 780 ampere capacitor inrush created a net neutral current of 620 amperes through relay 51N-9. Because 620 amperes exceeded the 240 ampere pickup, recloser R-9 locked out after only two fast operations. Synthetic North Feeder 9's 2,050 customers remained without power for 2.7 hours due to the failed restoration. No capacitor damage occurred because the bank fuse rated at 1,200 amperes did not melt under the 780 ampere inrush. Maintenance staff raised relay 51N-9's pickup to 800 amperes and enabled capacitor switching restraint logic. Only if bus residual voltage decays to zero for 30 seconds will breaker 52-9 be permitted to close.

synthetic_samples.reference_summary: The splice connector at Synthetic East joined an aluminium barrel to a stranded copper conductor. Galvanic corrosion formed a brittle oxide wafer at the dissimilar metal interface over years. No lightning discharge did strike the site; a capacitor bank switching transient did arrive. The transient voltage caused a small sparkover in the water layer at 14:32. The phase-to-earth fault current reached 11.4 kA on the 33 kV feeder bay. The feeder differential relay detected the increasing current imbalance within three cycles. The auxiliary transformer loss cut all HVAC power to the control room's switchgear. The battery charger stopped charging, so the 220 V DC substation battery carried the entire load. At 16:08 a hired 500 kVA mobile generator was connected to the essential 400 V board. Operating staff used the temporary generator to power the battery chargers and control loads.

semantic_core.text: The splice connector at Synthetic East joined an aluminium barrel to a stranded copper conductor.
Galvanic corrosion formed a brittle oxide wafer at the dissimilar metal interface over years.
The cable pit lacking drainage kept several centimetres of water around every splice.
No lightning discharge did strike the site; a capacitor bank switching transient did arrive.
The transient voltage caused a small sparkover in the water layer at 14:32.
The sparkover decomposed a track of the ethylene-propylene cable insulation into carbon.
The carbon track eventually bridged phase and earth, and a full ground fault started.
The phase-to-earth fault current reached 11.4 kA on the 33 kV feeder bay.
The feeder differential relay detected the increasing current imbalance within three cycles.
One pole of the circuit breaker opened, disconnecting Synthetic East from the grid.
After the breaker trip the 33 kV bus de-energised, stopping supply to the auxiliary transformer.
The auxiliary transformer loss cut all HVAC power to the control room's switchgear.
The battery charger stopped charging, so the 220 V DC substation battery carried the entire load.
After 45 minutes, the DC bus voltage had decayed from 243 V to 201 V.
The low-voltage lockout prevented the tie switch motor from closing the emergency feed.
In 2025 the planned splice thermal scan had been deferred but not cancelled.
At 16:08 a hired 500 kVA mobile generator was connected to the essential 400 V board.
Operating staff used the temporary generator to power the battery chargers and control loads.
After the generator ran, one repair crew replaced the splice with a copper compression connector.
The pit was fitted with drainage pipe and a partial-discharge monitor was wired to the alarm.

synthetic_samples.reference_summary: The 11 kV cable at Synthetic West had no protective concrete slab above its route. A detailed drawing claimed an 80 cm depth, but the actual cable was buried at 42 cm. No lightning discharge occurred; nevertheless, the live cable was struck by an auger bit. The auger's cutting tooth deeply gouged the cable's lead sheath and wrappings. The cable current swelled to 3.2 kA and tripped the overcurrent relay after a short time. The overcurrent relay sent a trip signal to the circuit breaker at the feeder's remote end. The essential lighting switched to emergency lamps that were not designed for full duty. Data terminal displays flickered when the DC control voltage dipped to 104 V. A 200 kVA mobile generator, brought from a nearby store, fed the essential AC bus at 16:45. With temporary power available, workers tested the cable and found the auger cut location.

Moisture from the wet soil easily reached the cable's exposed paper insulation.
The moisture allowed an electrical conduction path, and the phase insulation broke down into a ground arc.
The cable current swelled to 3.2 kA and tripped the overcurrent relay after a short time.
The overcurrent relay sent a trip signal to the circuit breaker at the feeder's remote end.
The circuit breaker opened, cutting off the 11 kV supply for station auxiliary power.
The station battery charger then lost its AC source, and the DC bus started to fall.
The essential lighting switched to emergency lamps that were not designed for full duty.
Data terminal displays flickered when the DC control voltage dipped to 104 V.
Two motorised disconnector controls refused to act because the undervoltage lockout engaged.
The transformer hall temperature reached 41 °C as cooling fans stayed stopped.
The site supervisor relied on grass appearance instead of locating cable before work.
A 200 kVA mobile generator, brought from a nearby store, fed the essential AC bus at 16:45.
With temporary power available, workers tested the cable and found the auger cut location.
They removed the damaged length and jointed in a new 11 kV cable with a cold-shrink splice.
Concrete covers, sand layers, and marker tape were placed at the corrected burial depth.

synthetic_samples.reference_summary: The zone 1 impedance setting of the protection relay was 6.0 ohms, while the actual line impedance was 12.5 ohms. The automation logic lacked a directional check for distinguishing a reverse fault from a forward fault. A lightning bolt struck the Synthetic Alpine feeder conductor at 14:23, creating a phase-to-ground fault. A second lightning stroke at 14:25 initiated a phase-to-phase fault on the same feeder. Because of the incorrect setting, the relay erroneously localized the phase-to-ground fault to the distant line section. The erroneous localization produced a trip signal that opened the healthy loop tie sectionalizer, not the faulty one. Approximately 300 customers were without power for 210 minutes after the healthy lateral was misisolated. The repeated overcurrents shortened the life of the main line cable by an estimated 4.5 years. Protection engineers calibrated the relay distance zone to match the actual 12.5-ohm loop impedance. The automation firmware was upgraded to include a directional angle blocking element for fault isolation.

synthetic_samples.reference_summary: The Ethernet link between Synthetic Creek and Synthetic Lake had a latency of 800 ms, exceeding the automation's 100 ms limit.
